send() returned <= 0 mid-write (peer closed or timeout); the byte stream is no longer reliable

error_codes.message: Network endpoint is not a valid address: '{detail}'
error_codes.hint: Pass a bare IPv4/IPv6 address (IPv6 may be bracketed); keep the port in its own argument and use Endpoint::local for UnixSocket paths or named pipes
The caller cancelled this operation (or its owner went away); the completion still fires once with this code, so drop the result only if the owner is gone

error_codes.message: This network capability is unavailable on the current platform
error_codes.hint: Query aurora::net::Engine::capabilities() before using it; this leg has no file-descriptor wait semantics (e.g. wasm), so there is no silent fallback by design. When a TLS backend factory reports it, the code names the configuration that backend cannot express (e.g. a system certificate store leg given an in-memory PEM identity): under the default candidate chain the next backend is tried, while an explicitly designated one (TlsContext::backend) returns it as-is

error_codes.message: URL is not a valid absolute or resolvable reference: '{detail}'
error_codes.hint: Pass a complete URL with scheme (e.g. https://host/path) or a reference to resolve against a base URL; percent signs must introduce a two-hex-digit escape and IPv6 literals need brackets

Fix the value instead of ignoring it: a proxy URL is scheme://[user[:pass]@]host[:port] with no path, and a NO_PROXY entry is *, a domain, a domain with :port, or an IPv4/IPv6 CIDR; a malformed proxy setting must never fall back to a direct connection

error_codes.message: This proxy protocol is not supported by the current build
error_codes.hint: Use http:// (HTTP/1.1 CONNECT), socks5:// or socks5h:// for the proxy itself; a TLS-protected proxy connection (https://) and SOCKS4 are not implemented, so do not silently downgrade to a plaintext proxy hop

error_codes.message: Proxy tunnel could not be established: '{detail}'
error_codes.hint: The proxy answered (or refused) but no tunnel was built; connect never fell back to direct on purpose, so check the proxy host/port and its own uplink rather than the target host

The proxy demanded authentication that was absent or refused: 407 on HTTP CONNECT, or a non-zero status on the SOCKS5 username/password subnegotiation; supply credentials in the proxy URL or re-authenticate once, do not retry blindly

The peer answered with bytes outside the CONNECT or SOCKS5 grammar (wrong version, missing status line, oversized header block); an HTTP hop is usually a captive portal or a plain HTTP server where a proxy port was expected

error_codes.message: Host name could not be resolved: '{detail}'
error_codes.hint: The resolver returned an error or an empty answer for that name; a numeric literal (IPv4 dotted form or bracketed IPv6) never reaches the resolver, so use one when DNS itself is the thing under test

error_codes.message: Operating-system proxy settings could not be read: '{detail}'
error_codes.hint: The channel exists on this platform but the read was refused (registry access, dynamic-store failure); this is distinct from a machine that simply has no proxy configured, and the library never treats the two as the same outcome

error_codes.message: Network policy refused the request before any byte went out: '{detail}'
error_codes.hint: A declarative NetPolicy dimension (cleartext allow-list, TLS version floor, or require-proxy) rejected this target; the detail names the dimension and both sides of the conflict. Widen the policy, add the host to allow_cleartext_hosts, or raise the TLS context's floor to match the policy — the request itself is unchanged and retrying it as-is cannot succeed

error_codes.message: Socket option or shutdown call failed: '{detail}'
error_codes.hint: setsockopt / getsockopt / shutdown returned an error (bad handle state, unsupported option, or the peer already reset the connection); the native code is in the message, check the option name and whether the socket is still connected

The non-blocking connect did not produce a result within the configured deadline; a black-holed peer or an unreachable route looks identical to a slow one from here, so retry with a longer StreamOptions::connect_timeout or fall back to another candidate address

Backpressure fired: pending bytes reached the high-water mark, pending reads exceeded the read-buffer cap, or a framed message overflowed its limit; slow the producer down or raise the matching StreamOptions field rather than dropping data

error_codes.message: Framed message exceeds its configured limit: '{detail}'
error_codes.hint: The stream produced a single message larger than FrameOptions::max_frame_bytes, or a length prefix declaring more bytes than the limit allows; raise the limit only for a protocol that genuinely carries such frames, otherwise treat the stream as malformed and close it rather than resynchronising inside an oversized frame

A Framer factory was given a limit of 0, an empty or oversized delimiter, or a length field width outside 1..8 bytes; framing must be configured before it is used, because a silent default here would either accept unbounded frames or split messages at the wrong place

error_codes.message: Socket option conflicts with the current configuration: '{detail}'
error_codes.hint: Two settings cannot both hold on one socket (a connected UDP socket receives only from its peer, so joining a multicast group there would configure a socket that can never receive the group); use a second socket for the other form rather than reordering the calls

The peer aborted or refused the negotiation (unsupported cipher suite, alert from the server, truncated handshake, or a plaintext endpoint answering on a TLS port); the transport is unusable after this and must be closed. Reproduce with the peer's TLS logs before changing TlsContext, because retrying the same parameters only reproduces the same alert

Chain verification failed (unknown issuer, expired or not-yet-valid leaf, hostname mismatch, or a policy constraint). Install the issuing CA into the trust root used by this TlsContext, or point TlsContext::add_trusted_certificate at the right PEM; do not reach for allow_insecure_certificate, which turns a real man-in-the-middle signal off for the whole transport

TlsContext::min_version rules out every version the peer is willing to speak (commonly a TLS 1.3-only floor against a 1.2 endpoint). Lower the floor deliberately and record why, rather than mirroring the peer automatically: the floor is the negotiated security baseline

Call aurora::net::available_tls_backends(): an empty list means this build compiled no TLS engine, so supply a provider through AURORA_NET_TLS_PROVIDERS=<static|shared>:<install root> or register a backend with aurora::net::register_tls_backend(). A non-empty list means the candidate chain matched nothing instead: check set_default_tls_backends() and TlsContext::backend, whose id must be one of the listed backends. Aurora never downgrades a TLS request to plaintext

The peer's certificate does not carry any pinned public key, so the pinned identity changed (key rotation, reissued certificate, or an interception proxy). Update the pinned SPKI digests from an out-of-band source you trust and rotate them in lockstep with the service; never fall back to allow_insecure_certificate, which defeats the pin entirely

error_codes.message: HTTP request cannot be sent as written: '{detail}'
error_codes.hint: The request violates the message grammar before any byte is written (unknown method text, a header name outside the token charset, a header value containing CR or LF, or a target URL without a host). Fix the request at the call site; the peer never sees it, so retrying with the same fields reproduces the same rejection

The detail names which of the three stages expired (connect, read_idle or total), and they mean different things: connect says nothing answered, read_idle says the body stalled mid-flight, total says the whole exchange overran. Raise only the stage that fired - a blanket total budget turns slow-but-healthy transfers into failures

error_codes.message: HTTP redirect chain exceeded the configured limit: '{detail}'
error_codes.hint: Either the peer is bouncing between targets or the limit is genuinely too small for this endpoint's chain. Inspect the Location sequence in the diagnostics before raising the limit, because following a cycle also leaks credentials to each hop it revisits

error_codes.message: HTTP response body exceeds the configured limit: '{detail}'
error_codes.hint: The guard is what keeps a wrong URL (a video behind a shortened link) from exhausting memory. The detail says which ceiling was crossed: max_body_bytes bounds the bytes that arrived on the wire, max_decompressed_bytes bounds the transparently decompressed payload (the decompression-bomb guard). Raise the one that fired if the payload is legitimately large, or switch to open_stream so the body is delivered in bounded chunks instead of materialized

error_codes.message: HTTP response charset is not supported: '{detail}'
error_codes.hint: Response::text() decodes only UTF-8 and Latin-1 in this batch, so a body labelled with any other charset cannot be turned into text here. The undecoded bytes are always reachable through body(), so transcoding is the caller's to do; do not silently substitute U+FFFD or reinterpret the bytes as UTF-8, which would corrupt the payload

error_codes.message: HTTP peer violated the message grammar: '{detail}'
error_codes.hint: The response is not parseable as HTTP/1.1 (bad status line, a chunk size that is not hexadecimal, framing that declares both Content-Length and an unknown Transfer-Encoding, or a body longer than its declared length). Close the connection and re-issue on a fresh one, because the byte stream is now misaligned and no later response on it can be trusted

error_codes.message: HTTP response content encoding is not supported: '{detail}'
error_codes.hint: The peer applied a content coding this client cannot undo - either the coding name is outside the advertised set (brotli and zstd are not built here) or the build was configured with AURORA_ENABLE_COMPRESSION=OFF, in which case no decoder exists and the request deliberately never advertised Accept-Encoding. Re-request with an encoding you can decode (Request::header sets Accept-Encoding; an identity body always arrives undecoded); never reinterpret the compressed bytes as text, which would hand the caller garbage

error_codes.message: HTTP response body cannot be decoded: '{detail}'
error_codes.hint: The message framed cleanly but its payload did not survive the declared content coding: the gzip/zlib/deflate stream is corrupt, truncated mid-symbol, or fails its trailing checksum. This is a data defect (at the peer, or in the encoding chain it declared), not a transport fault - the bytes arrived whole, so retrying the same target only re-fetches the same broken payload; check the declared Content-Encoding chain before suspecting the link

error_codes.message: No native web engine runtime available: '{detail}'
error_codes.hint: The WebView control degrades to a placeholder rectangle; install the platform runtime (WebView2 Runtime on Windows, libwebkit2gtk on Linux) to enable it
The engine runtime was found but could not be started; the control degrades to a placeholder - check the user data folder and display connection
Check the URI scheme and network reachability; custom schemes and file access must be enabled explicitly
The page may not have finished loading, or JavaScript is disabled on this control; retry after navigation completes
Snapshot mode needs a live engine and, on Linux, an available GTK display connection; use Interactive mode on X11 or Windows instead

error_codes.message: Web view not bound to a native host: '{detail}'
error_codes.hint: The control is rendering outside a window host (headless/offscreen) or was registered before the host installed its thread-local slot

error_codes.message: Web view mode unsupported on this backend: '{detail}'
error_codes.hint: Interactive mode needs a native child surface; Wayland and headless backends cannot host one - switch to Snapshot mode or move the control
Register the semantic name through IconRegistry before referencing it, or pick one of the registered names reported alongside this error
Register the icon font through FontEngine::register_font (or register_font_from_memory) and make sure the code point exists in that face

error_codes.message: Icon SVG source uses unsupported features: {detail}
error_codes.hint: The built-in rasterizer covers an SVG subset only - simplify the source or rasterize it outside the library and supply the bitmap

error_codes.message: HTTP request body cannot be sent a second time: '{detail}'
error_codes.hint: A 307 or 308 redirect must replay the message body, and the streaming body said it cannot return to its starting point, so resending it would ship a half-consumed payload. Either hand the payload over as an in-memory body, or make the source restartable (re-open the file and reset its cursor); note that a body which cannot restart also opts this request out of the retry policy on purpose

The peer ran the close handshake, a pong deadline expired, or this side shut the handle down, so no further frame will be delivered. Reconnecting is a fresh connection with a fresh handshake, not a resume: application-level state the protocol carried (subprotocol, session identity, anything the server keyed on the old connection) has to be re-established by the caller

The peer did not answer the upgrade with 101 Switching Protocols, Sec-WebSocket-Accept did not match the key this side sent, or a required subprotocol went unchosen. This is a stable answer about the endpoint and the configuration, so retrying the same request reaches the same verdict: fix the URL, the subprotocol list, or the Origin the server expects

error_codes.message: WebSocket peer violated the frame grammar: '{detail}'
error_codes.hint: A frame was malformed, exceeded a configured frame or reassembled-message limit, carried a control frame that is not a complete message or whose payload is longer than 125 bytes, or held text that is not valid UTF-8. The byte stream is now misaligned, so the connection is dropped rather than continued: no later frame on it can be trusted

The producer outran the wire: pending outgoing payload reached its byte cap or the queue its entry cap. This refuses only the message that hit the limit and leaves the connection open, on purpose - whether to keep buffering, drop, or close is the caller's decision. Slow the producer down or raise the matching WebSocketOptions field

The provide callback registered through the lazy offer returned an error, or was empty while the format was actually requested. The bytes could not be rendered on demand - fix the provider or supply the format eagerly; re-reading the same clipboard reproduces the same failure, so this is not a transient one

error_codes.message: This platform cannot listen for clipboard changes: '{detail}'
error_codes.hint: No clipboard-change listener mechanism exists here (the platform anchors are AddClipboardFormatListener on Win32, QClipboard::dataChanged, GdkClipboard::changed, and NSPasteboard changeCount). The absence is stable, so retrying cannot create it - sample available_formats() at the moments that matter instead of registering a listener that would never fire

error_codes.message: System drag payload read failed for '{mime}': '{detail}'
error_codes.hint: The source session went away, cancelled mid-transfer, or the bytes never arrived within the read deadline. Unlike a missing mechanism this is transient - the same format may well succeed on a second attempt - so surface the failure with a non-cursor fallback and let the control decide about retrying

error_codes.message: System drag payload could not be decoded as '{mime}': '{detail}'
error_codes.hint: The bytes arrived but do not form a valid payload for the declared MIME (for example image/png that no decoder accepts). The same bytes fail again - this is a data defect at the source, not a transient one; drop the payload and report it rather than retrying

The user pressed Esc, moved the pointer away, or the system ended the session. This is user intent, not a fault - do not route it into an error branch; the source data stays untouched and the control simply returns to its idle state

error_codes.message: Move drop landed but the source could not delete its data: '{detail}'
error_codes.hint: The target received and stored the payload, but deleting the original failed (file locked, permission revoked). The target's copy stays authoritative - retry the deletion later instead of re-copying, and remember the contract: the source never deletes before the move confirmation arrives

error_codes.message: Message catalog binary magic mismatch (expected AUM1)
error_codes.hint: The file is not an AUM1 message catalog. Check that the path points to the .bin produced by gen_i18n, not a JSON source or a different asset

error_codes.message: Message catalog binary version {version} is not supported (expected 1)
error_codes.hint: The catalog was produced by a newer gen_i18n. Regenerate the .bin with the tool version that matches the library

error_codes.message: Message catalog binary is not little-endian (version field decoded as {version})
error_codes.hint: AUM1 catalogs are little-endian only. Regenerate the file instead of byte-swapping it

error_codes.message: Message catalog binary truncated at offset {offset} (needed {needed} more bytes)
error_codes.hint: The file is shorter than its own header claims. Re-transfer or regenerate the .bin; do not attempt to salvage a partial file

error_codes.message: Message id range [{base}, {end}) collides with the invalid-id sentinel or overflows
error_codes.hint: The vocabulary id space must stay below AURORA_INVALID_MESSAGE_ID_VALUE and cannot wrap. Lower --id-base or split the vocabulary

error_codes.message: Vocabulary range [{base}, {end}) overlaps an already registered range
error_codes.hint: Two catalogs claim the same id space. Regenerate with disjoint --id-base values (builtin reserved range starts at 0, applications default to 1024)

error_codes.message: Message name '{name}' is already registered by another vocabulary
error_codes.hint: Canonical names are global. Rename one of the colliding keys in the JSON sources and regenerate

error_codes.message: Unknown message name '{name}' (not in any registered vocabulary)
error_codes.hint: add() resolves names through registered vocabularies. Load the vocabulary that owns the name first, or use the generated MessageId constant directly
